ShortDescription.Value: Copy & paste props — select, move, rotate, blueprint and stamp groups of props

Publish.LongDescription:
## Copaste A copy & paste tool for props — select groups of props, copy them, and stamp them anywhere with preserved layout, rotation and height.
## Features - **Click & marquee selection** — click props or drag a camera-aligned box; live highlight while dragging. Works on props, decals AND trees - **Copy & paste with preview** — the copied group follows your mouse as a ghost; click to place, repeat to stamp - **Move** — drag a selected prop to move the whole selection - **Group rotation** — hold right mouse button and drag, or use the panel buttons - **Height controls** — raise/lower (PgUp/PgDn), snap to ground (End), match another prop's height (Home) - **Delete** — press Delete to remove the whole selection at once. Combined with marquee + type filter it's great for bulk cleanup: box-select an area, press T on a tree to keep only that tree type, hit Delete — a whole overgrown forest gone in three clicks (and Ctrl+Z brings it back, ages preserved) - **Type filter** — press T to toggle a filter taken from the hovered/selected prop: marquee then only picks that exact type (works for trees too). While the filter is active, clicking any prop switches the filter to that prop's type - **Undo** — Ctrl+Z reverts move, rotate, height, delete and paste (32 steps); deleted trees come back with their original growth stage - **Blueprints** — save prop groups to disk and reuse them in any city or save - **Anarchy-style pasting** — ignores overlap errors while pasting (toggleable). Anarchy is NOT required: if it happens to be installed, Copaste additionally protects pasted props from being hidden by the game - **Toolbar button + panel** — clickable buttons for every action, with tooltips - All hotkeys rebindable, English and Serbian localization
## Usage Activate with **Ctrl+Shift+C** or the toolbar button. Click or drag-select props, **Ctrl+C** to copy, **Ctrl+V** to paste, click to place. Quick right-click steps back.
## Transparency AI-assisted development: the code was written with heavy use of AI tools (Claude Fable), directed, reviewed and hand-tested in-game by the author through many iterations. Full source code is public on GitHub (link below) — judge it freely. Bug reports are read and fixed by a human.
## Credits & thanks Copaste started as a personal tool and grew into this release. It stands on the shoulders of the CS2 modding community — written from scratch, with patterns and APIs learned from open-source mods whose MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses explicitly welcome that. Sincere thanks to:
- **yenyang** — the selection, highlighting and raycasting patterns were learned from the sources of *Better Bulldozer*, *Anarchy*, *Tree Controller* and *Move It*; Anarchy's PreventOverride is integrated at runtime when present - **algernon** — the object placement approach (the game's definition pipeline) was learned from the sources of *Line Tool* - **Bruceyboy24804** — *Node Controller* served as the reference for how mod UI integrates with the game's interface - **Colossal Order & Paradox** — for Cities: Skylines II and the official modding documentation - The **CS2 modding community** for keeping their mods open source — none of this would exist otherwise
### Special thanks A very special thank-you to **Biffa** (Biffa Plays Indie Games) and **ConflictNerd** — simply for being the author's favorite Cities: Skylines YouTubers and the reason this game never gets boring. Keep the traffic flowing!
Source code (MIT): https://github.com/viktorsx/Copaste
Publish.ChangeLog: - Fixed blueprint saving: Save now stores what is currently selected (it used to silently re-save the old clipboard content instead) - Blueprints now save tree growth stages (older blueprint files still load fine) - Loading a blueprint while already pasting now correctly refreshes the preview to the new group - Pressing Ctrl+V in the middle of dragging a prop no longer leaves the tool in a broken move state - Raised props now keep their height reliably after being moved or nudged - Selection overflowing the 1000-prop limit no longer leaves extra props permanently highlighted - Copaste no longer suppresses the game's error indicators on unrelated objects while pasting, and plays nicer with Anarchy's own error toggle - Blueprint names are validated more strictly - Small performance improvements in the panel and selection overlays
